utterances.text: These weapons were found at the headquarters of the KLA in Racak. That's my voice that you can hear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What are the dates that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are the list of duty officers, who was on duty according to the days; who was on duty when. This is a bunker and sand sacks. We found them up on the hill. Sandbags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are they empty sandbags?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, full. Full of sand. This is a tripod for the machine-gun, for the machine-gun nest with ammunition below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance to the trench or bunker, and it was the size of a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned uniforms here. Now you mentioned the KLA headquarters in your running commentary. You mention also the roster with dates when different people were on duty.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we found all this evidence, and we inventoried all of it. The on-site investigation was attended by OSCE representatives, all of it, and you can hear my voice explaining what we found to them, and you can hear the interpreter. There was a large number of the press and the media, foreign as well as local. This is our vehicle. When we came under fire, a bullet came through the windshield. You can see the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That is it. Mrs. Marinkovic, we saw part of this film on your activities on the day of the 18th. In this connection, you wrote a report on on-site investigation, Exhibit D4, which follows immediately after D3 relating to 15th to 17th January. Exhibit D4, which is already in evidence as well, was exhibited also during the testimony of General Drewienkiewicz. Mrs. Marinkovic, did you have occasion to follow the testimony of Witness Buja Sukra, or, rather, Shukri Buja? He was Mr. Nice's witness. He was a KLA commander from Racak.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no time to follow everything except for rare occasions in the afternoon when I'm free.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We can see in the transcript that he said that during the entry of the police, their duty officer, who was manning a machine-gun, opened fire at the police from a 12.7-millimetre machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this report on the on-site investigation, which is very brief, two pages only, it says that those attending included Danica Marinkovic investigating judge, deputy public prosecutor Dragomir Zivic, SUP inspectors Dabic Dragan and Srecko Dogandzic, scene of crime officer Sasa Bozinic, commenced at 1400 hours. And then you write that OSCE representatives were there all the time, two American nationals, Gil Gilbertson and Ed Sullivan, as well as an Italian Giovanni Fantini, as well as an interpreter from English into Serbian, Arta Ramaj. Professor Sasa Dobricanin as forensic expert from the Institute of Forensic Medicine in Pristina was also present. You then say that inside the mosque in the centre of the village 40 bodies were lined up, 39 male and one female. They were marked, photographed, filmed by video camera in the presence of the team members and OSCE observers. They were loaded on a truck with orders to transport them to the Institute of Forensic Medicine in Pristina for an autopsy. That's what you ordered to be done.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You then go on to say in the yard of an unknown house owned by an unknown person, a grenade for a hand-held launcher was found, a Chinese-made -- with a Chinese-made fuse. Camouflage uniforms were found, and so on and so forth. Chinese-made ammunition. I shall skip the specification of the supplies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, unless there is a specific point, it's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I wish the following to be established and commented on by Judge Marinkovic, because it hadn't been specified before: On the surrounding hills, trenches were found, and inside the trenches utensils for digging were found. All around the trenches there were empty cartridges for 7.62-millimetre Chinese weapons. Later on there is mention of bunkers, this anti-aircraft machine-gun, 12.7-millimetre Chinese-made bullet casings. You toured all the trenches. What was their combined length?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went around all the hill, and we went alongside trenches all the way. They were so long that we were unable to measures their total length, there were so many of them. Those trenches as we went from the foot of the hill all the way led us to the top where we found a machine-gun nest and a bunker. Along the sides there were also other trenches coming from all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't tour the entire length of the trenches but you mention in your report that there were many bullet casings and cartridges for Chinese-made weapons, and we know well that there was a time when the Republic of Albania bought weapons and arms from China in the '70s. Did you have any more precise information about when those weapons were transported from Albania into Serbia, Kosovo more specifically?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, even before this incident in Racak we had knowledge, both I and the prosecutor, that Racak was a stronghold of terrorist gangs. For many days, six months prior to that, they continuously brought in weapons from Albania to Racak. Racak is located in a hilly area surrounded by villages Petrovo and Malopoljce from which terrorists came into Racak and concentrated there and put up resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We need not dwell on this report any longer. You can remove it from the ELMO. In this film we saw your scene of crime team and OSCE representatives. Did anyone from outside, in addition to you, attend the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th, in addition to our team and OSCE representatives, there were many representatives of foreign and local media.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that already. Was there anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who you mean. I can't think of anyone at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't mean anyone in particular. I'm just asking.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the officials of our investigating authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned already in your report who attended; OSCE representatives, your team, the press, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you issue an order for an autopsy to be conducted on all the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I issued the order for post-mortems to be conducted, but before that I issued an order for a forensic expert team to be established to include the most eminent experts from our country; from Belgrade, Nis, Novi Sad, and Pristina. In my order, I specified their names. All of them were highly qualified experts, professors and doctors, very well known in their respective areas of expertise. In my order I specified all the steps to be taken, including those that need to be taken by forensic experts regarding post-mortems on the bodies found earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did that expert team perform what was required by your order?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was their duty and they complied with my order in every respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Later on a team of Finnish pathologists came in and joined the effort.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, before that our team was assisted by experts from Belorussia who had been there for a while. They were involved from the beginning. And later on, the Finnish experts came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you anything about the forensic expert aspect of the investigation because you yourself are not a professional. Just tell me, what was the result of that international cooperation between our experts, Finnish, and Belorussian ones?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They worked together, performed post-mortems on all bodies with the proviso that the Finnish experts came in later. But for the part of the autopsies when the Finns had not arrived yet, those bodies were autopsied again, reviewed again in the presence of the Finnish experts and all the findings were agreed and approved by them. There were 40 bodies in total and it was established that they had been killed by gunfire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we have to stop here --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- from a distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have to stop here today. It's the end of today's session, and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
